definition: Simulates Self-Healing Code Runtimes operating for a day.
description:

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where healing monitors monitoring, runtime logistics redundancy, or fault injection maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Self-Healing Code Runtimes Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Self-Healing Code Runtimes: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Self-Healing Code Runtimes — runtimes patching their own failures live.

Phase 1 — Prove (healing monitors): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (runtime logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (fault injection): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (patch verification): runtime hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and production-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
